completion_promises.criterion_text: study-tutor serve-nats --help prints flag surface matching --nats, --agent-id, --log-level.
completion_promises.evidence: Three click.option decorators (--nats, --agent-id, --log-level) on serve_nats() in src/study_tutor/cli/main.py. test_serve_nats_help_lists_required_flags asserts all three flag names appear in --help output and the command exits 0. The coach validation grep `study-tutor serve-nats --help | grep -E '(--nats|--agent-id|--log-level)'` returns matches for all three.

completion_promises.criterion_text: study-tutor serve-nats --nats nats://localhost:4222 starts the adapter, blocks until SIGTERM, then shuts down cleanly.
completion_promises.evidence: _serve_adapter() awaits adapter.start(), installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers via loop.add_signal_handler() (with NotImplementedError fallback), awaits a shared shutdown_event, and on completion runs adapter.stop() in a finally block followed by runtime_shutdown(write_helper). The CLI body wires --nats into config.nats.url before calling _build_nats_runtime() and runs the lifecycle via asyncio.run(_serve_adapter(...)). Verified by test_serve_adapter_starts_then_stops_when_shutdown_event_is_set, test_serve_adapter_registers_sigterm_and_sigint_handlers, AND the new BDD scenario (features/nats-fleet-integration/test_nats_fleet_integration.py: 'SIGTERM during an in-flight tutor turn drains the request before deregistration') which exercises the full SIGTERM path end-to-end through _serve_adapter.

completion_promises.criterion_text: SIGTERM during a running tutor process triggers adapter.stop() and the process exits with code 0 within the drain window (30s).
completion_promises.evidence: Signal handlers registered for SIGINT and SIGTERM both call _request_shutdown(), which sets shutdown_event. The wait()->finally branch awaits adapter.stop() (NATSAdapter owns the 30s drain window per TASK-NATS-PH1-005 scope) before runtime_shutdown(). On the happy path no SystemExit is raised so click reports exit code 0. The BDD scenario 'SIGTERM during an in-flight tutor turn drains the request before deregistration' (@task:TASK-NATS-PH1-006 in nats-fleet-integration.feature) is the load-bearing regression guard: a fake adapter starts an in-flight tutor_turn task, the When-step sets shutdown_event (SIGTERM-equivalent), and the Then-steps assert the in-flight task completed, the result was published, and the registry entry was removed, all within 30s. test_serve_adapter_registers_sigterm_and_sigint_handlers also pins the signal handler registration.

completion_promises.criterion_text: If nats-core's AgentConfig validation fails (e.g. invalid NATS_URL), the CLI exits 1 with a clear error message.
completion_promises.evidence: _load_agent_config() wraps any AgentConfig() construction failure in a typed _AgentConfigValidationError. The serve_nats body catches that exception, emits '[study-tutor] Error: AgentConfig validation failed: {exc.cause}' to stderr (preserving the underlying pydantic field names), and raises SystemExit(1). _serve_adapter additionally exits 1 when adapter.start() raises (with a separate banner and a best-effort stop()). Verified by test_serve_nats_exits_1_when_agent_config_validation_fails and test_serve_adapter_exits_1_when_start_raises.
